messages:
aj: getting a bunch of alerts — tool-router p95 jumped from ~180ms to ~420ms, p99 ~1.1s for function-calling + structured-output routes. Started ~1h after deploy. Noticed increased CPU on router pods and high time in json schema validation traces.

priya: saw same on the prod graph. Alerting page: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/abc123/tool-router-latency (p95/p99 panels). Affects customer A and some internal smoke tests.

emma: repro steps i used locally:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-structured-1","input": "<long prompt>","tools":[{"name":"search","schema": {"type":"object","properties": {"q": {"type":"string"}, "opts": {"type":"object","properties": {"filters": {"type":"array"}}}}}}]}'
```
Logs for a single request (trace id t=trace-9012):
```
[router] recv req -> 2ms
[router] route/dispatch -> 18ms
[schema-validator] compile/validate -> 720ms
[model-proxy] forward -> 85ms
[kv-cache] lookup -> 12ms
[router] assemble/stream -> 310ms
total -> 1147ms
```
Based on traces the heavy part is schema-validator (~700ms) for deeply nested tool schemas.

sam: we shipped tool-router v2.3.0 ~58m before alerts. That release added stricter per-tool JSON schema validation and switched to the python jsonschema lib for consistency. If validator is blocking request pipeline that's our prime suspect.

aj: can we toggle validation off quickly on high-throughput routes? Maybe a canary with validation disabled to confirm.

ops-oncall: I can push a hotfix to canary to disable validation for 2% of traffic for 10m. Will monitor p95/p99 and CPU. Applying patch now to clusters: canary/region-us-east.

priya: other quick mitigations to consider:
- disable validation on internal/default routes where we can accept looser structures
- add precompiled validators instead of runtime compile (jsonschema has slow compile path)
- migrate validation to async background step (validate after model returns and fall back to lax parsing)
- revert v2.3.0 if rollbacks are acceptable for customers impacted

emma: additional notes: our schema set is large (200+ tool schemas) and some have recursive/nested definitions. Precompiling with `fastjsonschema` or using AJV (node) dropped validate times from 600ms -> ~5ms in spike tests. We should benchmark switching validator impls in staging.

sam: agreed. Short-term: ops-oncall canary, if improvement confirmed we'll roll the config change to 20% then full. Medium-term: replace runtime python jsonschema with precompiled validators (or AJV) and add a compile-time CI step.

infra-bot: canary deploy started by ops-oncall at 3621456790. Run id: deploy-canary-3621456790.

ops-oncall: canary results after 10m: p95 dropped from 420ms -> 190ms, p99 from 1150ms -> 260ms on canary slice. CPU on canary routers reduced ~40%.

aj: that's pretty decisive. Plan: 1) continue traffic ramp for disabled-validation patch to 50% over next 15m, 2) open follow-up engineering ticket to replace validator library and add precompile, 3) add an emergency toggle in router config. I'll create RLW-3247 and assign to @sam + @priya.

priya: created RLW-3247: "tool-router: p95/p99 regressions due to runtime JSON schema validation; implement precompile + emergency toggle". Added reproducer, logs, canary graphs, and recommended rollback plan.

sam: i'll own the validator replacement RFC and coordinate with eng-runtime. Will add benchmark matrix (fastjsonschema vs ajv vs compiled Go validator) and a rollout plan.

emma: leaving notes here — for support: if you see customers hitting this, tell them we've deployed a canary fix and we're ramping; encourage customers to file minimal schema examples if they have complex tool schemas.

aj: thanks everyone. tagging @eng-runtime and @support on the follow-up. Will update thread as we ramp. :thumbsup:
